claim: PX4 (main docs) Offboard mode follows setpoints 'provided by some source that is external to the flight stack, such as a companion computer' over MAVLink/MAVSDK or ROS 2 (uXRCE-DDS or Zenoh); PX4 requires a continuous 2 Hz 'proof of life' stream and on loss (COM_OF_LOSS_T) switches out of Offboard and lands or runs the failsafe set by COM_OBL_RC_ACT; generic offboard modes 'bypass all internal PX4 control loops and should be used with great care'; PX4 cannot distinguish ROS 2 messages from internal ones, so conflicting writes can be 'possibly catastrophic'

ArduPilot developer docs: companion computers 'interface and communicate with ArduPilot on a flight controller using the MAVLink protocol', 'gather and pre-process information from advanced sensors' and make decisions during flight; listed hardware includes Raspberry Pi and CM4/CM5 baseboards, Holybro Pixhawk Jetson Baseboard, ARK Jetson PAB Carrier, Aerium Lumen (Jetson) and ModalAI VOXL2; the page does not itself state where failsafes live

EASA open-category page: the 'open' category is for leisure and low-risk commercial drone activity, with subcategories A1/A2/A3; drones must carry a C0-C4 class label, be privately built or have been placed on the market before 2023-12-31; class rows set a 120 m altitude limit; 'All drones operating in the open category (with limited exceptions) need to be equipped with a remote identification system'; 'specific' (medium risk) and 'certified' (high risk) categories exist
